notes: מִתּוֹךְ is split rather than fused because the ASV spends *from* on the preposition and *among* on the construct noun, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is unmet and the subtraction test leaves each morpheme with a rendering of its own; the contiguous בְּתוֹךְ later in the verse is fused because one English word carries both.
כִּי אֵין לוֹ בֵּן follows rule 43's verbless possessive: *no* on אַיִן (rule 50), *had* on the preposition, *he* on the suffix.
The Sh token of תְּנָה is a cohortative/paragogic he with no English realization (rule 32), not a directive Sd.
